````text
# #5289: Patch: write the card data JSON one record per line, about 260k fewer lines
Opened by @MaxGoetzmann.

## Why

The repository holds about 2.8M tracked lines. About 334k are JSON, and most of that is card data pretty-printed by `serde_json::to_string_pretty`, which gives every field, and every tag in an array, a line of its own. A delta that changes 317 cards takes 9,776 lines (`crates/cards/patches/deltas/v0.2.0.json`). Writing each **record** (a card, a patch row, a version row) as one compact line keeps diffs and merges at the level of one card, and makes a `grep` for a card id return its whole entry in one hit. In return the tree shrinks by roughly a tenth.

This changes how the files are formatted, not what they contain: every file must parse to the same `serde_json::Value` as before.

## The files, measured (lines now → after)

| File(s) | Now | After | Record |
|---|---|---|---|
| `crates/cards/catalog.json` | 45,922 | ~1,236 | each card under its id |
| `crates/cards/patches/patches.json` | 38,737 | ~290 | each element of the top-level array |
| `crates/cards/patches/deltas/*.json` (288 files) | ~114k | ~cards changed + 3 per file | each card under `"set"`; `"unset"` on one line |
| `crates/cards/patches/technical.json` | 11,090 | ~1,577 | each element of the array |
| `crates/cards/patches/index.json` | 5,048 | ~981 | each id's array |
| `crates/cards/patches/records`, `win_rates`, `card_metrics` | ~38k | small | each row / version entry |
| `analysis/fixtures/dev-40.report.json` | 12,998 | ~271 | each game / row |
| `apps/web/src/audio/voice-manifest.json` | 7,638 | ~1,912 | each line's entry |
| `crates/cards/chinese.json`, `flavour.json` | ~10k | ~2,470 | each id |

The total measured across the tree is about −264k. **Leave `bot/` alone** (`bot/go/internal/commands/testdata/python.json`, −11k): it is in the night bot's `forbidden_paths`.

## What to build

1. **One writer.** Add a "record per line" serializer beside `stringify_pretty` in `crates/tools/src/patches.rs`. The shape is: wrapper objects and arrays open and close on their own lines, each key down to the record level on its own line, and each record as compact JSON (`serde_json::to_string`, keys in their existing order) on a single line, ending with a trailing newline. Choose the record depth for each file family to match the table above, and name each depth as a constant (rule 9).
2. **Every writer uses it.** Route each place that writes one of these files through it: `write_json` (20 call sites in `patches.rs`), `retcon.rs`, `winrates.rs`, `technical.rs` (writes `technical.json` with `to_string_pretty` directly), `catalog.rs`, and `apps/web/scripts/gen-voice.mjs` for the voice manifest. Also whatever writes `analysis/fixtures/dev-40.report.json`. Leave `stats.rs`, `perf.rs`, `gate.rs` and the other writers of reports that aren't in the table as they are, unless they write one of these files.
3. **Rewrite the files once** with the new writer: a one-off `cargo jackioh` pass or a test that writes and compares. It must not be a hand edit.
4. **A check that keeps it (rule 15).** Add a scan to `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs` that fails when any file in the table is not byte-identical to the writer's output for its parsed value. That way the next `to_string_pretty` can't bring the old format back.
5. **Readers stay as they are.** Everything that reads these files parses them as JSON (`crates/cards/build.rs`, the tools, `apps/web/scripts/github-releases.ts`, `analysis/jackioh_records`, `releases.yml`'s `git show … patches.json`). No reader needs a change, but confirm it and say so in the PR.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Every rewritten file parses to the same value as on `main`. A test proves it for every file in the table, by comparing against the file's `git show origin/main:` copy, or by round-tripping it through the writer.
- [ ] The new acceptance scan fails on a pretty-printed copy of any of the files and passes on the tree.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh catalog check`, `cargo jackioh patches check` and `cargo jackioh spec check` pass.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims` reports no card that plays differently and asks for no fragment. Because the content is unchanged, the PR is `kind:internal`.
- [ ] The golden replays and `cargo jackioh fuzz --seeds 200` pass unchanged: what `build.rs` folds from the deltas is the same.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, the workspace tests and the web's tests pass.
- [ ] The PR body gives the line count before and after (`git ls-files -z | xargs -0 wc -l | tail -1` on both).

## Notes

- `.gitattributes` already routes `*.json` through mergiraf, which merges JSON by structure, so one card per line should cause no more conflicts than now. Two branches editing **different fields of the same card** will now touch the same line. Say in the PR if that changes anything for `patches cut`/`ship` on `main`.
- `scripts/ci-scope.sh` maps these paths by name. Leave its mapping as it is.
- This is step 1 of a plan to remove about 500k lines. Step 2, moving the 75 MB of rendered audio out of git, needs a person to choose R2 or LFS and isn't part of this issue.

```rust
const INDENT: &str = "  ";
fn is_space(c: char) -> bool { matches!(c, ' ' | '\n' | '\r' | '\t') }
fn is_mark(c: char) -> bool { matches!(c, '{' | '}' | '[' | ']' | ',' | ':') }
fn opens(token: &str) -> bool { matches!(token, "{" | "[") }
fn closes(token: &str) -> bool { matches!(token, "}" | "]") }
/// Each mark, each string whole, each other literal; white space dropped.
fn tokens(json: &str) -> Vec<&str> {
    let mut tokens = Vec::new();
    let mut chars = json.char_indices().peekable();
    while let Some((start, c)) = chars.next() {
        if is_space(c) { continue; }
        let mut end = start + c.len_utf8();
        if c == '"' {
            let mut escaped = false;
            for (at, d) in chars.by_ref() {
                end = at + d.len_utf8();
                if escaped { escaped = false } else if d == '\\' { escaped = true } else if d == '"' { break }
            }
        } else if !is_mark(c) {
            while let Some(&(at, d)) = chars.peek() {
                if is_space(d) || is_mark(d) || d == '"' { break; }
                end = at + d.len_utf8();
                chars.next();
            }
        }
        tokens.push(&json[start..end]);
    }
    tokens
}
fn new_line(out: &mut String, level: usize) { out.push('\n'); out.push_str(&INDENT.repeat(level)); }
pub fn layout(json: &str, depth: usize) -> String {
    let tokens = tokens(json);
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(json.len());
    let mut open: Vec<bool> = Vec::new();
    for (at, token) in tokens.iter().enumerate() {
        let rest = &tokens[at + 1..];
        if opens(token) {
            let wraps = open.len() < depth
                && if open.is_empty() {
                    rest.first().is_some_and(|next| !closes(next))
                } else {
                    rest.iter().find(|t| opens(t) || closes(t)).is_some_and(|t| opens(t))
                };
            out.push_str(token);
            open.push(wraps);
            if wraps { new_line(&mut out, open.len()); }
        } else if closes(token) {
            if open.pop() == Some(true) { new_line(&mut out, open.len()); }
            out.push_str(token);
        } else {
            out.push_str(token);
            if open.last() == Some(&true) {
                match *token { "," => new_line(&mut out, open.len()), ":" => out.push(' '), _ => {} }
            }
        }
    }
    out.push('\n');
    out
}
```
````

```rust
fn is_space(c: char) -> bool { matches!(c, ' ' | '\n' | '\r' | '\t') }
fn is_mark(c: char) -> bool { matches!(c, '{' | '}' | '[' | ']' | ',' | ':') }
fn opens(token: &str) -> bool { matches!(token, "{" | "[") }
fn closes(token: &str) -> bool { matches!(token, "}" | "]") }
/// Each mark, each string whole, each other literal; white space dropped.
fn tokens(json: &str) -> Vec<&str> {
    let mut tokens = Vec::new();
    let mut chars = json.char_indices().peekable();
    while let Some((start, c)) = chars.next() {
        if is_space(c) { continue; }
        let mut end = start + c.len_utf8();
        if c == '"' {

                end = at + d.len_utf8();
                if escaped { escaped = false } else if d == '\\' { escaped = true } else if d == '"' { break }
            }
        } else if !is_mark(c) {
            while let Some(&(at, d)) = chars.peek() {
                if is_space(d) || is_mark(d) || d == '"' { break; }
                end = at + d.len_utf8();
                chars.next();
            }
        }
        tokens.push(&json[start..end]);
    }
    tokens

                    rest.first().is_some_and(|next| !closes(next))

            if open.pop() == Some(true) { new_line(&mut out, open.len()); }
            out.push_str(token);
        } else {
            out.push_str(token);
            if open.last() == Some(&true) {
                match *token { "," => new_line(&mut out, open.len()), ":" => out.push(' '), _ => {} }
            }

    }
    out.push('\n');
    out
```

```rust
const INDENT: &str = "  ";
fn is_space(c: char) -> bool { matches!(c, ' ' | '\n' | '\r' | '\t') }
fn is_mark(c: char) -> bool { matches!(c, '{' | '}' | '[' | ']' | ',' | ':') }
fn opens(token: &str) -> bool { matches!(token, "{" | "[") }
fn closes(token: &str) -> bool { matches!(token, "}" | "]") }
/// Each mark, each string whole, each other literal; white space dropped.
fn tokens(json: &str) -> Vec<&str> {
    let mut tokens = Vec::new();
    let mut chars = json.char_indices().peekable();
    while let Some((start, c)) = chars.next() {
        if is_space(c) { continue; }
        let mut end = start + c.len_utf8();
        if c == '"' {
            let mut escaped = false;
            for (at, d) in chars.by_ref() {
                end = at + d.len_utf8();
                if escaped { escaped = false } else if d == '\\' { escaped = true } else if d == '"' { break }
            }
        } else if !is_mark(c) {
            while let Some(&(at, d)) = chars.peek() {
                if is_space(d) || is_mark(d) || d == '"' { break; }
                end = at + d.len_utf8();
                chars.next();
            }
        }
        tokens.push(&json[start..end]);
    }
    tokens
}
fn new_line(out: &mut String, level: usize) { out.push('\n'); out.push_str(&INDENT.repeat(level)); }
pub fn layout(json: &str, depth: usize) -> String {
    let tokens = tokens(json);
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(json.len());
    let mut open: Vec<bool> = Vec::new();
    for (at, token) in tokens.iter().enumerate() {
        let rest = &tokens[at + 1..];
        if opens(token) {
            let wraps = open.len() < depth
                && if open.is_empty() {
                    rest.first().is_some_and(|next| !closes(next))
                } else {
                    rest.iter().find(|t| opens(t) || closes(t)).is_some_and(|t| opens(t))
                };
            out.push_str(token);
            open.push(wraps);
            if wraps { new_line(&mut out, open.len()); }
        } else if closes(token) {
            if open.pop() == Some(true) { new_line(&mut out, open.len()); }
            out.push_str(token);
        } else {
            out.push_str(token);
            if open.last() == Some(&true) {
                match *token { "," => new_line(&mut out, open.len()), ":" => out.push(' '), _ => {} }
            }
        }
    }
    out.push('\n');
    out
}
```

## Risks

- **Table sharing (R5268001).** `write_table` compares bytes. Ship's `lists_text` must use the new layout, or every ship writes a duplicate file.
- **Replays and fuzz.** `build.rs` compacts the catalog and parses the deltas. The values don't change, so no hash moves.
- **gen-voice.** `voice.yml` commits the manifest, so the JS port must match the Rust layout byte for byte. The JS test holds that, and step 12 makes a voice PR run `rust_tools_wasm`.
- **Hand edits.** catalog.json is edited by hand. A card entered in two-space form fails CI until someone runs `format-json`; the docs say so.
- **Merges.** Two branches changing different fields of one card now touch the same line. mergiraf merges JSON by structure, so `patches ship` and `cut`, which write deltas, `patches.json` and `index.json` only on `main`, are unaffected.
